clue.text: Result in race

definitions.meaning: to result in something is to produce or give rise to it
a race of animals is a strain or variety of them

explanation.surface: Someone reporting the outcome of a running race.
explanation.definitionFit: To breed trouble is to cause it, and a breed is a distinct strain or stock of animal.

clue.text: Programme about to get under way in summertime

indicators.note: in places the joined pieces inside the summertime abbreviation

parts.note: BST stands for British Summer Time

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece getting under another is placed below it, so it follows in the answer

parts.note: a road is a way
CA is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A show is about to start during the summer season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get under' works in this down clue: about sits below way. BST, British Summer Time, is the UK's daylight-saving clock period.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio or television transmission is a programme sent out over the air.

clue.text: Winter and rough weather, perhaps, under the greenwood tree (A.Y.L.I.)

definitions.text: Winter and rough weather, perhaps, under the greenwood tree (A.Y.L.I.)

parts.words: Winter and rough weather, perhaps, under the greenwood tree (A.Y.L.I.)
parts.note: the song in As You Like It says that under the greenwood tree one shall see no foe but winter and rough weather

explanation.surface: A quotation recalling the woodland song from Shakespeare's As You Like It.
explanation.walkthrough: A.Y.L.I. is As You Like It; Amiens' song 'Under the Greenwood Tree' runs 'Here shall he see / No ___ / But winter and rough weather.'
explanation.definitionFit: In the song, winter and rough weather are the only foe or adversary to be faced in the forest.

clue.text: Telephone about raising bribes for an elimination

indicators.note: about means the telephoning word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to dial is to telephone

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word lifts it so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: sops are small bribes given to pacify

explanation.surface: Someone phones about lifting bribes to get rid of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' reverses the bribes word, as this is a down clue, and 'about' wraps the telephone word around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Disposal is the getting rid or removal of something, which is what an elimination does.

clue.text: The prayer before a rosary ends often takes minutes

parts.note: the Secret is a prayer said quietly by the priest in the Roman Catholic Mass

indicators.note: the ends of the word rosary are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A churchgoer's prayer said before the rosary, often running for minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minutes' is not about time: it means the written record of a meeting, which the official keeper usually takes.
explanation.definitionFit: A committee's clerical officer records the proceedings of meetings in written notes.

clue.text: Spring break

definitions.meaning: to spring is to move suddenly, like a trap or a sprung catch shutting
to break suddenly, as a twig does

explanation.surface: A short holiday taken in the springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap can spring shut with a sudden sound, and a twig can crack in two with that same sharp crack.

clue.text: Writer in nonconformist sect? Not her!

indicators.note: nonconformist suggests letters refusing to stay in their usual order

explanation.surface: Asking whether a writer belongs to a dissenting church, and saying it is not a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonconformist' looks like a description of the sect but rearranges SECT NOT HER; G.K. Chesterton was an English author, famously Catholic.
explanation.definitionFit: G.K. Chesterton was an English author of the Father Brown detective stories.

clue.text: Going furtively to the border

definitions.meaning: a decorative trim or fringe along an edge

explanation.surface: Someone sneaking off towards the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: One creeps sideways by inching along, and a trim sewn round a garment is its fringe.

clue.text: Donald would be a dead duck without it!

definitions.text: Donald would be a dead duck without it!

parts.words: Donald would be a dead duck without it!
parts.note: Donald Duck is a cartoon character who only moves because of the drawn process that brings him to life; a dead duck also means a hopeless case

explanation.surface: A remark that Donald Duck would be finished without something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dead duck' is an idiom for something doomed, but here it is literal: the cartoon Donald is lifeless without the process that makes drawings move.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartoon films are made by this technique of filming drawings in sequence to give the illusion of life.

clue.text: Submit return

definitions.meaning: to submit is to give way
a return is the profit an investment gives

explanation.surface: An instruction to hand something in and get something back.
explanation.definitionFit: To give way is to surrender, and a profit produced by an investment is its output.

clue.text: Make too much of rubbish written in old poetry

indicators.note: written in means one word is set inside the other

parts.note: verse is poetry
tat is cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: A critic exaggerating how bad some old verse is.
explanation.definitionFit: To exaggerate a point is to claim more for it than is warranted.

clue.text: In conversation, men give this appearance

indicators.note: in conversation means the word for men is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: guys is an informal word for men

explanation.surface: Men talking together and giving a certain impression.
explanation.definitionFit: An outward semblance or form, often a false one, is how something looks.

clue.text: The right way to go about getting fungi

indicators.note: to go about means the joined words turn round and read backwards

parts.note: a Tory belongs to the political right in Britain
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A political right-winger telling us the correct way to forage for mushrooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go about' turns TORYRD round. Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry rot is wood decay caused by certain fungi, so the name stands for those organisms.

clue.text: A guide to colours

definitions.meaning: a benchmark or norm against which things are measured
a regiment's colours are its flag

explanation.surface: A handbook explaining which colours to use.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm used for measuring is a benchmark, and a military flag carried as an emblem is also called by this word.

clue.text: New Royal advantage?

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN for Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Asking whether the monarchy has gained a fresh edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges R with ADVANTAGE, and the whole clue also defines it: the newest, most experimental art is new, and its letters are a royal advantage made over.
explanation.definitionFit: Experimental, innovative art and ideas are described as ahead of their time, ie new.

clue.text: Criticize main motion in bill

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the advertisement word

parts.note: a bill is a poster or advertisement

indicators.note: motion means the letters of main are set moving into a new order

explanation.surface: Attacking the chief proposal tabled in a parliamentary bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motion' scrambles the word main, and 'in' sets the result inside the bill word just after its first letter; 'main motion' poses as a parliamentary term.
explanation.definitionFit: To animadvert on something is to pass censorious comment on it.

clue.text: Popular star on the rise becomes a trend-setter

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it, so comes first

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a nova is a star that suddenly brightens
a tor is a rocky hill or rise

explanation.surface: A rising pop star becomes a style leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in this down clue puts NOVA above TOR. 'on the rise' looks like one phrase about fame; the rise is a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who introduces new methods or fashions leads where others follow.

clue.text: Order start of advance in attack

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the word for attack

parts.note: a fit is a sudden attack of illness

indicators.note: the start of advance is its first letter

explanation.surface: A command to begin an advance during an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiat is an authoritative decree or command.

clue.text: Toy boy, perhaps, put on show

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece put on another is placed above it

parts.note: a Teddy boy was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress, so boy can follow teddy
to bear marks or signs is to show them

explanation.surface: A young lover, a toy boy, being put on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toy boy' reads as a young lover, but Toy is the definition and 'boy, perhaps' hints at Teddy boy, the 1950s British youth cult.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffed plush bear is a classic children's plaything.

clue.text: A female faces insults

parts.note: fronts are faces, as of buildings

explanation.surface: A woman confronts insults.
explanation.definitionFit: Affronts are open slights or offences to someone's dignity.

clue.text: Container vehicle

definitions.meaning: a large receptacle for liquid or gas

explanation.surface: A lorry carrying a large container.
explanation.definitionFit: A tank holds water or fuel, and it is also an armoured battlefield vehicle on tracks.

clue.text: A foreign criminal, punished but still free

parts.note: un is French for a
a con is a convict, a criminal
fined means punished with a money penalty

explanation.surface: A foreign offender was fined rather than jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: A punishment that is only a fine leaves the criminal out of prison, which the surface trades on.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not shut up or restrained remains at liberty.

clue.text: Without restrictions, boars wander in Provence

indicators.note: without means the letters of the restrictions word are taken away from boars

parts.note: bars are restrictions
to range is to roam or wander

explanation.surface: Wild boars roam freely in the south of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' removes B, A, R, S from BOARS, leaving O. Orange is a town in Provence, famous for its Roman theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange is a historic town in the Vaucluse department of southern France.

clue.text: The purchase of influence

definitions.meaning: purchase here is mechanical grip or advantage, as with a lever
power to sway people or events

explanation.surface: Buying political sway.
explanation.definitionFit: The mechanical advantage of a lever gives grip, and figuratively the same word means power to sway outcomes.

clue.text: Politician gets a favourable vote up country

parts.note: Lib is short for a Liberal politician

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ay is a variant spelling of aye, a yes vote

explanation.surface: An MP wins a vote in favour, up and down the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AY into YA in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Libya is a nation in North Africa.

clue.text: Horrible sound to bear

indicators.note: sound to means the bear word is heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a grizzly is a North American bear

explanation.surface: A bear's frightening noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gruesome causes horror or disgust.

clue.text: Set task for a flyer …

explanation.surface: A duty assigned to a pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: A stint is a small wading bird related to the sandpiper.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotted portion of work is a shift, and the dunlin's small cousin the wader bears the same name.

clue.text: … a flyer engaged in some activity

parts.note: a tit is a small bird, a flyer

explanation.surface: A bird busy doing something, continuing the previous clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots carry on from the previous clue, so 'a flyer' is reused with a new sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hard at work or busy is the idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Staff avoid dismissal

definitions.meaning: in cricket, to ... is to keep batting without being out

explanation.surface: Employees keeping their jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter who is not dismissed continues to bat, so carries on batting.
explanation.definitionFit: A conductor's stick or a relay runner's rod is this, and a cricketer not out continues at the crease.

clue.text: Tenacious but misguided veteran without a tie

indicators.note: misguided means the letters are led astray into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A stubborn old soldier wrongly going without a necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misguided' rearranges VETERAN and TIE, with 'without a' telling you to leave out the A first.
explanation.definitionFit: Retentive means holding on firmly, as a good memory keeps facts.

clue.text: Understanding unruly male teenager

indicators.note: unruly means the letters behave badly and fall out of order

explanation.surface: Coming to terms with a badly behaved adolescent boy.
explanation.definitionFit: An understanding between parties is a pact or accord they have reached.

clue.text: Kept in safe deposit — a rare instrument

indicators.note: kept in means the answer is held inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A rare musical instrument stored in a safe-deposit box.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked Indian stringed instrument.
